listenings.text: Good morning, and welcome to the annual symposium on emergency and trauma care. A few practical notes before we start. Registration is open until eleven, and your badge gives you access to all the rooms on the second floor. The first panel begins at nine thirty, and the presenters have asked for questions at the end, not during the talk. Coffee is served at eleven in the main hall, and lunch is at one. One more thing: the networking session this evening is optional, but if this is your first symposium, go. Most attendees say they learn more in that room than in any of the talks.

Hi, this is Greg Sanders. I got your email last week, and I am sorry for the slow reply. I have been traveling. I read your message about the trauma database, and yes, I would be happy to talk. I collaborate with two groups in South America already, so this is familiar territory for me. Two things before we speak. First, send me the two-page summary you mentioned. Second, tell me what you want from the collaboration: data, co-authorship, or a place in the lab. People rarely say that out loud, and saying it saves everybody a lot of time. Talk soon.
